front: Relative mass and charge of a proton, neutron and electron
back: Proton: mass 1, charge +1. Neutron: mass 1, charge 0. Electron: mass ≈0, charge −1.
Atomic number = number of protons. Mass number = protons + neutrons.

front: What evidence led to the nuclear model of the atom?
back: The alpha particle scattering experiment — most particles passed through gold foil, but some deflected or bounced back, showing a tiny, dense, positive nucleus.
Electrons exist in specific shells (energy levels) at set distances from the nucleus.
An atom of the same element (same protons) with a different number of neutrons.
They have full outer electron shells.

front: Why does reactivity increase down Group 1 (alkali metals)?
back: The outer electron is further from the nucleus, so less strongly held and easier to lose.

front: Why does reactivity decrease down Group 7 (halogens)?
back: It gets harder to gain one more electron as atoms get bigger (the outer shell is further from the nucleus).
